title: Can't pin GUI applications started by script
line: Apps whose launcher runs a wrapper script now show their own name and icon in the Task Manager and pin correctly.
explanation: When a desktop file's Exec is a wrapper script that starts the real program, the window's class and app id match no desktop file, so libtaskmanager fell back to the process command line and made up a service for the interpreter or binary (here 'python3'). The task got a generic icon, and Pin to Task Manager stored 'file:python3', which shows as a blank file icon once the window is gone. Apps launched from a desktop file run in a systemd unit named after it (app-<id>@<random>.service from KIO, app-<launcher>-<id>-<random>.scope from others). libtaskmanager now reads that unit from /proc/<pid>/cgroup and maps the window to that desktop file, but only when everything else running in the unit is a shell, so windows of programs started by another app (Steam games, IDE terminals) are not taken for that app.

commits.message:
libtaskmanager: match windows to the desktop file of their systemd unit

Apps whose desktop file starts them through a wrapper script showed a
generic icon and pinned a broken launcher. Also match the window by the
app-<id> systemd unit it runs in, when only shells run there with it.

BUG: 403666

media.caption: Current master: TeamSpeak-like app started from Kickoff through a wrapper script; the task has a generic X icon and its tooltip says 'python3'
With the fix: the task shows the desktop file's icon and is called 'TeamSpeak 3 Client'
Current master after Pin to Task Manager and closing the window: the pin is a blank file icon called 'python3' (launchers=…,file:///usr/bin/python3)
With the fix: the pin is the app (applications:teamspeak3.desktop) with its icon and name
Current master context menu: no 'Open New Window', Pin pins python3
With the fix: 'Open New Window' and Pin to Task Manager for the app
